text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Croatian kuna becomes official means of payment in the last rebel Serb enclave of Eastern Slavonia on Monday.
- Introducing a pension system in Eastern Slavonia is the next step for its reintegration under Zagreb rule, director of the state Pension Fund Damir Zoric says.
- Social Democratic Party (SDP) appoints Zdravko Tomac as their candidate for the presidential elections on June 15 and says there will be no coalitions with the ruling HDZ party.
- Zagreb money market introduces daily publication of Interbank Bid and Offered Rates based on interest rates quoted by nine banks.
- State oil company INA to sign an agreement on gas research in Central Adriatic with the Italian AGIP in 20 days, says INA executive director Marijam Pejcic.

- Rift deepens between two fractions of the strongest opposition party - Social Liberals. Its head Vlado Gotovac who rejects any coalition arrangements with ruling HDZ faces strong resistance among his ranks.
- Commentary: Croatian hotels are cheeper than Italian and Spanish, but food prices in shops are among the highest in the Mediterranean area.
- Social democrats (SDP) say they have decided to run independently at the presidential elections after opposition parties failed to agree on a common candidate. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
